summary: Iteration 53 — Sections 54 (EN i18n), 55 (Saved eCards: bookmark/like/note), 56 (OG dynamic previews). All 15 backend pytest cases pass; all critical frontend flows pass: save buttons on /p/:slug, bookmark→note modal→save→preview, like toggle (no modal), /mis-guardadas page with filters, self-save hidden on own profile, EN translation of header nav-saved aria-label + /mis-guardadas page title.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is now 9686 lines (was 9188 in iter 52) — well over the 700-line threshold. Sections 55 + 56 each added ~150 lines. The og_bot_middleware at the bottom runs on EVERY request — even /api/* and static asset requests pay the cost of the UA-substring check and path-prefix checks. Consider gating it on path early or moving SocialBot logic to an APIRouter mounted only on /p and /provider, or run it as a Starlette Route rather than a global middleware.
The /api/og/p/{slug} route returns 200 with cache-control headers for valid slugs but uses a plain HTMLResponse (no cache) for the 404 fallback — minor inconsistency.
_recompute_provider_save_counts does two count_documents queries + one update_one on every PUT/DELETE — fine at current scale but consider an aggregation/$facet to halve roundtrips when this grows.

Saved eCards list endpoint sorts by saved_at but never updates saved_at on re-save (only $setOnInsert) — so if a user changes a bookmark to a like and then to bookmark again, the list ordering reflects the ORIGINAL save time, which may surprise users. Consider sorting by last_updated_at instead, or expose both.

Public provider profile (GET /api/providers/by-slug/...) exposes like_count + bookmark_count to anyone — fine for likes but bookmarks are arguably more private. Confirm this is intentional product decision.

OG image SVG fallback when slug is missing still returns 200 (good for not breaking social previews), but the underlying React route /p/{bad-slug} likely shows a 404 page. Social bot would see a happy preview and humans would see 404 — slight UX dissonance.
The og_provider_html endpoint sets X-Robots-Tag: all — this is the inverse of noindex. Confirmed intentional but worth a comment in code so future engineers don't accidentally noindex it.

success_rate.frontend: 100% on testable flows (6/6 critical UI flows + 1 self-save guard + 1 EN translation aria-label)

For Section 56, the og_bot_middleware is registered on the FastAPI app but in the Kubernetes preview ingress routes /p/* to the React SPA, so the middleware never fires for browser requests — only /api/og/p/{slug} works directly via curl, which is by design (share components in the FE now construct shortUrls pointing at /api/og/p/...). All OG meta tags validated via WhatsApp UA. Frontend SaveECardButtons + SavedECardsPage testids match spec. Demo provider currently has like_count=1, bookmark_count=1 from the Playwright run — fine for next regression.
rca of the issue: No bugs to RCA — all backend endpoints return expected status + payloads, all frontend testids resolve, modal/preview/filter flows match the spec, and EN translations render correctly on /mis-guardadas (page title 'My Saved eCards', stat labels 'BOOKMARKED' / 'LIKED' / 'PRO TIP', filter buttons 'All' / 'Bookmarked' / 'Liked').
